headline: Not yet. But Korea's 5% chip crash on Tuesday 13 October is a crack.
summary: The Kospi fell 5.46% on Tuesday 13 October, SK hynix down 10% and Samsung 7%, as foreign money fled and China's CXMT threatened memory margins. Tokyo followed, SoftBank down 8.5%. US CPI lands Wednesday 14 October with the 10-year yield at 5.24%.

analysis: Asia's AI chip complex cracked on Tuesday 13 October. The Kospi closed at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, after falling 7.4% intraday to its lowest since late July. Samsung Electronics lost 7.39% and SK hynix 10.09% on reports that China's CXMT will ship server DDR5 chips by year-end, and foreign investors sold a net 2.2 trillion won, nearly 8 trillion won this month. [1][2] Tokyo followed: the Nikkei 225 fell 1.68%, Kioxia 13.28% and SoftBank Group, an OpenAI investor, 8.50%. Taiwan's Taiex fell 1.9%. [2][3]

The selling started in New York on Monday 12 October, when the Nasdaq slipped 0.44% to 27,246 as Sandisk fell over 6% and Micron 3.9%; Nvidia lost 1.3%, AMD 2.3% and Broadcom 1.9%. [2][4] The strain is showing up in financing: Broadcom is assembling a package above $50 billion with Apollo and Blackstone for custom OpenAI chips, Oracle is negotiating an off-balance-sheet structure with Apollo and Goldman Sachs for a 1-gigawatt data center, and SpaceX has sought $40 billion of debt for Nvidia processors. [7]

Rates are the other jaw. The 10-year Treasury ended Friday 9 October at 5.24%, and a Wall Street Journal survey of 71 economists found most expect it to stay above 5%, some seeing 6% next year. [4][5] The Fed's range is 3.75–4% after its 16 September hike; September CPI lands on Wednesday 14 October with headline inflation expected at 3.6%. [6][8] Why 76: a 5% one-day fall in the most AI-exposed major index, on rising competition and fleeing capital, is the first visible crack, so the score enters Critical. [1]
